short: The United States' first swept-wing jet fighter, famously matched against the Soviet MiG-15 over Korea.
full:
Introduced in 1949, the North American F-86 Sabre was the United States Air Force's premier daytime fighter during the early Cold War. Its swept-wing design allowed for near-supersonic speeds, giving it a critical performance advantage over earlier straight-wing jets. In the skies over Korea, it became the primary counter to the Soviet-built MiG-15, engaging in some of history's first large-scale jet-versus-jet air combat in "MiG Alley".

Over 9,800 Sabres were produced, making it one of the most widely manufactured Western jet fighters. It served in the air forces of over thirty nations, seeing combat in the Indo-Pakistani Wars and remaining in frontline service with several countries well into the late twentieth century. It was finally retired by the Bolivian Air Force in 1994.
